sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles. 2003. Makhuwa (P30). In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 546-568. Routledge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not mention Manyawa at all (checked by a full-text search for stress/accent and reading sec. 1); its Makhuwa tone description cannot be attributed to Manyawa.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Manyawa language (language-archives.org/language/mny, as of Jan 2025, via the Internet Archive).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and the two Shrum & Shrum survey reports (oai:sil.org:36525, 36550).

sources.citation: Guerois, Rozenn. 2015. A grammar of Cuwabo (Mozambique, Bantu P34). PhD dissertation, Universite Lyon 2.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on Manyawa prosody; sec. 1.3.1 p.7 only notes that Cuwabo speakers 'also identify Manyawa spoken around Lugela' as a variety, 'influenced by Lomwe due to its embedding within Lomwe-speaking area'; no Manyawa data.

sources.note: Manyawa appears only as a row in a speaker-percentage table (0.94%, from Ethnologue); no linguistic content on it.

sources.citation: Reiman, Duane. n.d. [c. 2001-2002]. Findings from the sociolinguistic survey of the Manyawa people. SIL Mozambique, unpublished ('report forthcoming' per Reiman 2002:6).

sources.note: The only first-hand fieldwork report on Manyawa (1997 survey); appendices contain Manyawa word lists and may contain transcription/phonology notes (tone or penult marking). Low odds of an explicit stress statement but it is the sole primary document.
